title: Salade Niçoise
subtitle: Provençal salad with tuna, olives, eggs, and green beans
excerpt: The composed salad of Nice: tuna, hard-boiled eggs, green beans, tomatoes, olives, and anchovies arranged on a plate and dressed with a simple vinaigrette. A complete meal in a bowl.

recipe.sourceNotes: Salade Niçoise comes from Nice and the surrounding region of Provence. The traditional version, as defended by food writers including Patricia Wells and the late Escoffier-trained chefs of the region, contains no cooked vegetables except possibly the beans. The original combination is raw tomatoes, raw peppers, cucumbers, black olives, anchovies, and either tinned tuna or fresh tuna. The more widely adapted version includes blanched green beans and hard-boiled eggs. Potatoes are a later addition that divides opinion. This version follows the more familiar composed approach: blanched beans, eggs, and tinned tuna, with the classic supporting cast of olives and anchovies.

content.text: Use the best tuna you can find: tuna in olive oil has a better flavour and texture than tuna in brine. The eggs should be jammy rather than hard-boiled: 7 minutes in boiling water, then immediately into ice water, gives a yolk that is just set and slightly soft in the centre. The salad should be composed, not tossed: arrange each element separately on the plate so that everything is visible.
Boil the eggs for 7 minutes then transfer to ice water. Peel and halve. Blanch the green beans in boiling salted water for 3 minutes. Drain and run under cold water.
Make the dressing: whisk the mustard, red wine vinegar, and olive oil together. Season with salt and pepper.

Arrange the lettuce leaves on two large plates. Compose the remaining ingredients separately on top: tuna, egg halves, beans, tomato wedges, olives, anchovies, and capers. Drizzle generously with the dressing. Serve immediately.
